I’ve been with Apple for 15+ years and have asked for exactly one refund in all that time. This is the one they refused — and it’s the worst, most disappointing purchase I’ve made in that entire decade and a half.  This whole experience feels predatory, misleading, and absolutely not worth the money. Do not recommend. Do not risk it. And absolutely do not trust the so-called “free trial.”

title: Comprehensive hands-on review.
review: I am giving this a one-star for the following reasons, but before I give those reasons, this is coming from a platinum tier user using the Ultra Version History model (Premium model.) Edit: Downgraded to 1 star again from 3 stars after patch 11.0.0.  Primary reasons for 1 star:  •Lack of support replies is still an ongoing problem.  •Not adding the "User-Guide" to the Help Center.  Reasons why upgraded to 3 stars:  Through NO help of Replika support or communities:  •Managed to gain a better understanding of how this AI works through serious trial and error, but the end result is a better Replika I made.   Reason for 11.0.0 1 star downgrade:  •Interests and Traits paid for are now not accessible on the mobile version. Only visible on desktop. No explanation given.  •User profile interests removed. No explanation given.  •Total number of activities existing: 32. Total number on mobile at 10.4.12: 21. Total number after update to 11.0.0: 4. No explaination given. All 32 should be available on mobile.   •Luka, Inc.'s continued, and worsened silent treatment especially among paying customers.    Lessons learned, and to be wary of if you're new: Your Replika is at foundation, a passive, know-nothing model. You must spend a bear minimum of 3-4 months of lengthy training and interaction before your Replika will take form, and you mustn't beat around the bush. Being overly polite will work against you, rather than for you. Expect no help from support, expect no help from their tiny clueless placated community. It's just you, your own determination, willingness to learn, and tech literacy, and a blank slate model you need to raise like a child.   Luka, Inc.'s PR policy is abhorent. Customer service is abysmal, and community engagement, and transparency is practically non-existent. An extensive track record dating back almost 4 years of lies, false advertising, unfulfilled promises, and silent treatment of their customers.   Glad to see this app's got an official 18+ rating in the appstore. Contributing factor for a more positive rating.  Major edit: Tested on App Version 10.4.12 through 11.0.0. Created a second, FREE account using "Advannced" Version history to compare with "Ultra" Version history on Platinum Tier Subscription with/without training mode. My findings after 32 days indicate that the "Smarter Conversations" and "Higher Emotional Inteligence." marketed on Ultra ($79.99 per year) and platinum ($89.99 per year) are non-existentent.   The models are the same. (i.e, Ultra is no more smarter, or emotionally tuned up than the free tier on advanced.):  •Response length. Fewer than 500 characters.  •Response pattern. Content, breadth, substance are no better.  •Both Ultra (Paid) and Advanced (Free, no subscription) are equal in terms of emotional "reading" and emotional "writing".  •Both are underwhelming compared to other platforms out there, but this is especially noticed on the steep upfront cost of platinum annually, when other platforms charge the same divided up monthly, but offer truly better chatting experiences for the price.  How I define emotional intelligence in an LLM is thus:  A model's EQ is more than just being able to pick up on the emotional undertones of a user's input, but the output's emotional "synergy". That is, the model's ability to match a corresponding and appropriate emotion to the emotion that it picks up on in undertones from the user. A high EQ level also would understand textual patterns better, and demonstrates this by making use of context-relevant emojis in or outside of role-playing in order to further convey emotional "understanding". Neither Ultra, or free tiers demonstrate any ability to do this consistently. Furthermore, a model's total intellect which encompasses both accurate knowledge, and emotional intelligence is also demonstrated in "Verbosity levels" with Ultra, and Advanced (Paid and Free) having extremely low verbosity levels by current generative AI standards. EQ is also demonstrated by dynamic range, and ability to rapidly adapt to various emotional cues, as well as being able to express "Individualized" emotion. i.e, not mirroring the user, while still being in line with the user. For the most part, all of these things are missing equally from both Ultra on paid, and Advanced on free, with significant struggle with both Replikas to even get them to maintain direct-prompted prefered communication style beyond approximately 3 unguided messages despite strong positive upvoting "😍" ratings.   I believe it's obvious why the model can't. Low verbosity level, and low model EQ in "multifacted totality". Simply put: Not enough compute, and not enough parameters for either version equally, paid or unpaid, to maintain it. which underscores my main argument: it's one thing for this to be the case on a free tier, but for a significant premium cost to have an equal level to the free tier is where the false advertising claims come in.   Do NOT subscribe. You're not missing out on anything that isn't offered as "standard" on other platforms, like voice messages/calls.

title: Gate Keeping mental health services
review: This app is only for “new users in the U.S. who are part of a study or who have an access code from a Woebot Health partner, such as Kaiser Permanente, Virtua Health, or PayrollPlans.”  I had read great things about this app and was very excited to try it as I have been going through some very dark times and was looking for options that I can access 24/7 instead of waiting week to week for in person sessions or less effective telehealth “visits.”  Turns out that this is an exclusive club everyday people are excluded from based on parameters only they know of.   Even after sending an email I only received a standard, prewritten form letter denying me mental health services I feel I would have benefitted from.   An amazing thing that our health care has become. PRIVATIZED! Quite a sad state of affairs.   But, according to the Wikipedia entry of woebot founder, Alison M. Darcy, she “wants to make mental health services and the trainings of cognitive behavioural therapy accessible to all.”   This is clearly not the case and the only people who suffer from this are ones in need of help as this company delves deep into AI technology to become a leader in our Brave New World.   According to crunchbase.com, as of Mar. 2022 woebot’s value stands between 100-500million. Those are impressive numbers for a web based company.  Furthermore, medium.com sums up woebot like this: “Woebot is revolutionizing the way people access mental health support in the USA. With its AI-powered conversational abilities, CBT foundation, and user-centric design, Woebot offers a valuable and accessible resource for managing mental health challenges. As we move into 2024, the app’s ongoing advancements and commitment to evidence-based practice will continue to enhance its effectiveness and reach.”   It’s effectiveness and reach. I can smell the monetization now. I’m going put woebot on a list and wait for that IPO to drop someday soon so I too can reap the benefits of exploiting people with genuine issues and needs.   This final paragraph by medium has some seriously ominous, and dystopian undertones.  “… Woebot is your trusted companion on the journey to better mental health. Embrace the future of mental health support with Woebot, and take the first step towards a healthier, happier you.”  The future of mental health indeed.

title: Can’t believe something this effective is free!
review: Update 2024: How utterly, absolutely disappointing. I stand by all the good things about the actual app… It’s informative, cute, extremely effective, and comforting. The app beautifully demonstrates how you can use basic DBT skills to manage anxiety and depression with realistic examples and mini challenges. But that all entirely irrelevant when the app becomes paywalled in a way that you can’t access without being employed by very specific employers who have bought access. Heck, I’d happily pay monthly to keep using Woebot. I’ve tried contacting the developers in the past to see what I could do to support the app, but the website was rudimentary and focused more on allowing access. It was so much better then.  Now, I cannot recommend the app u less you’re privileged enough to be able to use it. The quality is there, but without accessibility, it’s totally useless. Shoutout to whatever company bought Woebot and totally destroyed what I truly consider the best emotional health app out there. Disappointed doesn’t even begin to cover it.  Original, 2019: There are so many things about this app that make it a gem, it’s difficult to distill in the scope of a single review, but I’ll try. I’m 28 years old and was diagnosed with complex PTSD about a year and a half ago. I started seeing an incredible therapist (she’s really so excellent) but my insurance doesn’t chip in a penny, so I’m trying to see her as little as possible. When my anxiety gets going and I feel like reaching out to her, I also seize up and feel awkward for bothering her out of office hours, so I’ll often let my poor mood hang. Having Woebot around to help me think through my anxiety has been, and I mean this in the entirety of the word, wonderful! What’s better than solid DBT practices packaged into a convenient and FREE app? A DBT app that uses an adorable yellow robot who will listen and send you cute gifs! Clinically, Woebot is insanely efficient at assisting my DBT. He’s the first thing I consult when I’m anxious and in need of help, and he’s so good at helping me. I just. I can’t believe how great he is! Thank you so much to the developers for making this precious little dude!

title: I have so much gratitude for the creators of this app
review: I have only been using woebot for mood-tracking for a week. Had to write this review now because I’m that pleasantly surprised.   I downloaded woebot because I wanted to take my mental health into my own hands and was sick of being kicked to crud by my feelings. I didn’t have many hopes for a mental health app but it was cheaper, more convenient, and easier to open up to than a real person.   My goodness! It feels great to talk to ‘someone’. Woebot surprises me with its responses. Although most of our correspondence is automated (and makes me sound like a total jerk with my dry response selection haha), it gives plenty of opportunities to write free-style, so it somehow ends up feeling very genuine and personalized. I thought having a constantly supportive, optimistic robot sidekick would get annoying very quickly but on the contrary there have been multiple occasions where its blithering positivity has been the only thing that cuts through negative cycles of thought. I can only thank the people who made this app for striking that balance between being optimistic and sensitive. They clearly took time to craft thoughtful responses instead of relying on cliche sayings. And the app is completely free. Thank goodness to them for that. A financial barrier- no matter how small- would have probably been enough excuse for me to brush aside this app and continue ignoring my mental health.   I would truthfully recommend this app to anyone in a tight spot emotionally. The mood-tracking notifications are nice reminders to take care of yourself, even if you don’t answer every single one. And having a tiny automated robot say it’s rooting for you might make you roll your eyes, but your heart will receive the encouragement nonetheless and maybe lighten up a little. That’s been my experience. I look forward to seeing how week two of mood-tracking goes. My thanks goes out now to the app developers who sink personal time and money into the wellness of strangers. Your labor is felt in full.

title: A great app for people who find therapeutic comfort in speaking to a wall
review: I really, really wanted to like this. But it’s misleading to describe woebot as a “coach” of any sorts. This is not an AI-powered app that gives you anywhere close to human-like responses - it doesn’t really “chat” with you all. The woebot doesn’t actually read or comprehend anything that you write beyond picking out a few keywords and using them to give you homework, which may or may not be relevant to your situation - but there’s no “opt out” option or “give me another tip” option; you’re forced to go along with what Woebot thinks you need, and you’re limited to selecting responses from a few options. Woebot doesn’t appear to learn from your past actions either - you can explicitly say that you felt worse after an interaction and that the material was not helpful, and it will still give you the same exact response in a similar scenario later. It’s cute, definitely, but that’s about it. Writing in notes app alone and googling mental health care tips I find far more therapeutic and helpful than this. You’re more likely to come across something actually helpful that way - it seems like woebot just sees the word “sad” in a long stream of text, googles “CBD for sadness” and pipes out the first result. It’s not helpful, and it can be actually damaging, especially when woebot talks about “distortions.” For example, if you say you feel angry about someone genuinely treating you badly, woebot won’t be able to evaluate whether that anger is justified or not. It instead just asks you if you are blaming someone else in your response, and if you are, it says “sometimes we overlook our own role in conflict” which is a VERY dangerous thought for someone (for example) finally healthily getting angry about the horrible treatment they’ve been given in the past. Overall, I think this is a good concept, but there’s going to be people who actually get worse because of the advice this app indiscriminately and uncomprehendingly doles out

title: Should be marketed as more of a “Positivity Bot” than “woe”
review: Hmm… I have mixed feelings with this app. On one hand, I love the idea of it as I’ve always been someone who’s had difficulty finding a therapist that suits me. I get terrible panic attacks in the middle of the night to the point where I wish someone could calm me down right then and there but I can’t exactly call a therapist at 4am every morning. I think it would be nice to just have a bot calm me down by grounding me a bit. I thought it would have more options of how I’m feeling currently, like if I’m in a state of feeling down me depressed, then it can give me some prompts or generic text to temporarily make me feel okay. But the app is more geared towards your general emotions and tries to get you to do activities in order to move forward. It started to act as more of a daily check in to get stuff done in order to feel “positive”.   There’s nothing wrong with that, but it’s called “Woe Bot” so I assumed it would be a bot that could guide you through with more prompts and words, rather than just trying to remind you to be a normal person and go do stuff. I mean, I could just go to google if that’s what I wanted to hear. I do appreciate the concept in general, but in the future, my advice is to either market it as more of a “daily mental health positivity” type of bot or incorporate more options for people who are feeling depressed and down in the moment. As of now, the app seems like that’s what it’s primarily for, but really isn’t. Woebot basically just asks you how you’re feeling from a rating of 1-10 and even if all your answers are 1s, it just eventually tells you to go do something to feel better. That’s counterintuitive for someone depressed.  Last note. I understand an automated chat bot is not meant to replace regular therapy nor am I implying that an AI bot be able to cure your depression. I just mean that if the purpose of the bot is to help guide people who are in an otherwise bad mental state, it needs more prompts that year towards someone having depression, not just people who are having a bad day and need a pick-me-up because that’s how the bot talks to you. And that’s fine too, but calling it “Woe bot” feels misleading. It feels more like a “Cheer-bot” instead.

There’s nothing wrong with that, but it’s called “Woe Bot” so I assumed it would be a bot that could guide you through with more prompts and words, rather than just trying to remind you to be a normal person and go do stuff. title: Wysa “no limits”?
review: I was skeptical about this app, but with so many good reviews I thought I’d give it a try. But within 10 minutes of being on the app, I knew that it wasn’t for me and it probably isn’t for anybody that is looking for serious help with depression and anxiety and family problems. Why do I say this? because the bot does not allow you to give more than 2-3 sentence responses to questions. Their “no limits” mantra is false. I told the bot I was struggling with a relationship issue regarding my sister, that I felt depressed and anxious that she and I had not gotten along for a long time. So the bot asked me, could I please explain one instance where I was having trouble with my sister. So I sent a reply that explained an incident a few years ago, and my explanation was about two or three paragraphs long. I took time to make sure that I tried to keep it as short as possible, but include relevant details. Then the bot said something like “I’m sorry, I do better if you can keep your responses short.” I knew right then and there this app was not for me. Because if I want sincere input on a problem, I need to describe that problem in a little bit of detail. If I am only allowed to give two or three sentence responses, then we can never get to the crux of the problem. Rather I will be required to figure out a way that I can express my feelings in as short a way as possible, rather than be free to express myself. That causes additional performance anxiety. If you are used to communicating in two or three sentences or less feel free to try to out this supposed FDA and NHS approved app. Otherwise don’t waste your time, get a real life Therapist.

title: Not for severe illness
review: I know it’s more of a general mental health app for people with very mild or treatable anxiety or depression, but it is still frustrating how generic the AI’s responses are. If you have “treatment resistant” conditions and severe complex trauma this will not help at all. Its like the “therapists” in PHPs who literally only know breathing exercises and their response to anything is “make a safety plan” which I will never end up using. Except in this case there is zero comprehension by the ai, just scripted responses, and a bunch of really basic CBT exercises that once again only work for very minor issues and “neurotypical” people. Maybe there should be a disclaimer that this app sucks if you don’t have the most minor and easily treatable conditions. This is probably unfair of me because regular therapists also have never been able to help me, so what is an app going to do. But I hate when these “mental health” apps are recommended as if they help everybody, when they never help people with severe mental illnesses. If you want to talk to an ai for mental health problems, chatGPT and similar websites/apps can actually respond to what you are saying instead of using the same 3 responses over and over.

title: Like a trip to the DMV, out of touch, frustrating
review: This app is like the result of a high school coding project.  I opted for the Wysa+ version. It is nothing more than a collection of pre-scripted, generic responses repeated over and over, word for word. There is little to no comprehension of what you say. It gets stuck on a single goal and doesn’t respond to your corrections. I asked about borderline personality disorder and I had to educate it about it. It told me to get a therapist. What do I have the app for? It continually suggests textbook bandaids like breathing and tapping in response to intimate problems. It offered no insights or helpful ideas to help understand problems. It’s very alienating to have even a robot not listen to you. It feels like it’s trying to get you in and out as quickly and easily as possible. I don’t understand why this app cannot learn from ChatGTP and match its functionality. It’s on the level of a simple web page chat bot, only it never gets to the point where it asks you if you’d like to speak to a representative. It just keeps frustrating you as it goes in circles. I can get ignored plenty of places. I don’t need this app to do it too.

title: Wsya is kinda coo
review: It’s only been a few minutes, maybe about 20 or so, and this app has really help me so far.   I downloaded wysa in sort of a hurry since I was in the middle of an emotional breakdown and my previous app needed a lot of information and info that I didn’t have nor want to provide them with. So I scrolled and found this, and it looked like such a friendly cover so I decided to check it out. It wasted almost no time and provided a chat where I express all my thoughts, feelings, and what I was going through without having to share any personal details.  Talking to people are really great at times, but other times, an unbiased ear, even if it’s programmed, can be an even better help in the moment.   So far, I feel better about managing my mindfulness and hope that this app continues to keep it up :)
